status: Company claim — evaluation and rollout plan
title: A new text watermark approach has important limitations
lead: OpenAI described how a statistical mark might help identify some generated writing.
happened: On October 5, OpenAI published an explanation of its text watermarking approach. The company announced that selected API customers could opt in to the feature and outlined plans for eligible products in the European Union. The approach places subtle patterns into word choices that a detector can assess. The company's evaluations found that longer passages were generally easier to identify and that editing could reduce detection. Initial detector access was limited to approved researchers and organizations.
matters: Schools, publishers and readers increasingly want useful information about the origins of online writing. Watermarks can be one source of evidence when the system that created the text supports them. Their reliability depends on the writing, the detection method and subsequent edits.
limits: An absent watermark does not establish human authorship. A positive result is not an infallible conclusion. The announcement does not mean every AI-generated passage can be identified.
analogy: A manufacturer's mark can be useful without appearing on every product.
